videos.title: The Boötes Void: 330 Million Light-Years of NOTHING
videos.desc:
Three hundred thirty million light-years... of absolutely nothing. When I first learned about the Boötes Void — a region of space so empty it should not exist — I honestly had to sit down. In this episode of Cosmic Unknown, we journey into the Great Nothing: how astronomers stumbled on it in 1981, why only 60 galaxies live where 2,000 should be, the chilling thought experiment about what humanity might never have known, and the theories trying to explain the unexplainable.

Rogue Planets: The Dark Worlds Drifting Between Stars
videos.desc:
Imagine a world where the sun never rises — not because it is night, but because there is no sun at all. Astronomers believe trillions of these sunless worlds, called rogue planets, are drifting through our galaxy right now. In this episode of Cosmic Unknown, we explore how planets lose their stars, how we detect invisible worlds with gravitational microlensing, NASA's upcoming Roman Space Telescope mission, the mysterious JuMBO planet pairs found by James Webb, and the thrilling question: could life exist in hidden oceans beneath the ice of a world that has never seen daylight?
